Then regenerate or re-save the produced artifacts.

remedies.label: Request Changes

Otherwise ask "What should change?" and end the turn, then submit their answer the same way. Either way that unlocks revision and a fresh review.

remedies.label: Confirm the summary again
remedies.description: I'll show you the current summary of your answers for NFR Design to confirm, then save its documents again from it.
remedies.action: Present the current consolidated summary and record it with the checkpoint flags (a plain decision or answer never counts): `focus engine log decision --checkpoint summary-confirmation --stage nfr-design --questions-file '<path to nfr-design-questions.md>' --decision 'Does this all look correct?' --options 'Looks correct,Request changes'`, with exactly one blank `[Answer]:` line in the summary section; end the turn; after the human's fresh reply run `focus engine log answer --checkpoint summary-confirmation --stage nfr-design --questions-file '<path to nfr-design-questions.md>' --details 'Looks correct'`. Then regenerate or re-save the produced artifacts.

remedies.label: Stop working unattended
remedies.description: I'll stop working on my own and ask you what should change in NFR Design. This also throws away every Unit's finished NFR Design work, and each needs its review and approval again.
remedies.action: Halt unattended execution and ask a human what should change. Unset FOCUS_UNATTENDED, ask "What should change?" for stage "nfr-design", and end the turn. Only after the human answers may their exact text be submitted as the Request Changes reason. Construction runs one unit at a time here, so this also throws away every unit's finished "nfr-design" work: each unit that already did it does it again and needs its review and checkpoint approval again.

remedies.label: Turn this check off
remedies.description: I'll turn the state transition check off for this piece of work. It is recorded, and it comes back on for the next piece of work.
remedies.action: Turn the state-transition check off for this piece of work. After the command succeeds, tell the person in one line that it is off for this piece of work, comes back on for the next one, and that they can ask you to turn it back on; then retry what was refused.
remedies.command: focus engine config set guard.state-transition off

remedies.label: Confirm the summary again
remedies.description: I'll show you the current summary of your answers for Code Generation to confirm, then save its documents again from it.

Then regenerate or re-save the produced artifacts.

remedies.label: Start the stage over
remedies.description: I'll redo Code Generation from the top. Your answers are kept, but you'll confirm the summary again and I'll save each of its documents again. This also throws away the work every Unit has finished, and each needs its reviews and approvals again.
remedies.action: Restart the stage from the top with /focus --stage code-generation. This costs more than finishing the current revision: your recorded answers survive, but you re-confirm the summary once and then save every output document again, so each one descends from the new confirmation. Construction runs one unit at a time here, so this also throws away the work every unit has finished: each unit redoes its steps and needs its reviews, Plan Approvals and checkpoint approval again.

remedies.label: Turn this check off
